rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_MARKER
rows.values: Path of a file. The script only tests that the file exists.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `perfetto` sleeps for `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_DELAY` seconds before it exits.
rows.effect: Makes the fake `perfetto` wait until this file exists before it exits.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT` is not empty.

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_NOTIFY_STATUS
rows.values: The text `0` means success. Any other text means failure. The script compares text and does not parse a number.
rows.default: Unset: `0`, success.
rows.effect: Selects whether the fake `perfetto` reports readiness success or readiness failure on the `--notify-fd` descriptor.
rows.notes: With `0` the script writes a byte of value 0 and creates `perfetto.ready` in the `FAKE_STATE` directory. With other text it writes a byte of value 1. It then exits with `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT`, or with status 1 when that is empty.

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_QUERY_HANG
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: off. A `--query` call of the fake `perfetto` returns.
rows.effect: Makes any `--query` call of the fake `perfetto` never return.
rows.notes: The test also asserts that the file `query.called` does not exist. This proves that the launcher script `perfetto/tronperf` makes no `--query` call.

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_SERVICE_ERROR
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `perfetto` prints `Connected to the Perfetto tracing service`.
rows.effect: Makes the fake `perfetto` print `Service error: Duplicate buffer name` in place of the connected message.
rows.notes: The script still writes the readiness byte. Then it waits until `runtron.args` or `killall.args` exists in the `FAKE_STATE` directory. Then it exits with status 0.

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_SKIP_NOTIFY
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `perfetto` writes the readiness byte.
rows.effect: Stops the fake `perfetto` from writing a readiness byte to the `--notify-fd` descriptor.
rows.notes: The script then does not create `perfetto.ready` in the `FAKE_STATE` directory. `FAKE_PERFETTO_NOTIFY_STATUS` then has no effect. The test sets it to check the readiness timeout of the launcher script `perfetto/wrapper`.

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_WAIT_FOR_PROBE_EXIT
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `perfetto` does not wait.
rows.effect: Makes the fake `perfetto` wait until the fake `traced_probes` process has ended before it reports readiness.
rows.notes: The script reads the process id from `traced_probes.pid` in the `FAKE_STATE` directory. It stops waiting when `/proc/<pid>/stat` is not readable, or when that file shows the state `Z` (the process has exited).

rows.name: FAKE_PR_BASE_SHA
rows.values: Text. The script prints it unchanged. The test passes a commit id of 40 characters.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `gh` stops with an unbound-variable error on `pr view`. The script runs with `set -euo pipefail`.
rows.effect: Gives the base commit id that the fake `gh` prints in its `pr view` answer.
rows.notes: The test runs the CI script `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh close-stale-pr` with the fake `gh` first on `PATH`.

rows.name: FAKE_REMOTE_SHA
rows.values: Text. The scripts print it unchanged. The tests pass a commit id of 40 characters.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `git` or `gh` stops with an unbound-variable error. The scripts run with `set -euo pipefail`.
rows.effect: Gives the commit id that the fake `git` prints for `ls-remote` and the fake `gh` for `pr view`.
rows.notes: Two tests set it. One test changes the value between two runs of the CI script `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh dispatch-required-ci`. It checks that the second run fails.

rows.name: FAKE_RUNTRON_DELAY
rows.values: Number of seconds. The script passes the text to `sleep` unchanged.
rows.default: Unset: 0.05 seconds.
rows.effect: Sets how long the fake `runtron` sleeps before it exits.
rows.notes: It has no effect when `FAKE_RUNTRON_HOLD` is set.

rows.name: FAKE_RUNTRON_EXIT
rows.values: Exit status, an integer. The script passes the text to `exit` unchanged.
rows.default: Unset: exit status 0.
rows.effect: Sets the exit status of the fake `runtron`.
rows.notes: It has no effect when `FAKE_RUNTRON_HOLD` is set. The test sets `37` and checks that the launcher script `perfetto/tronperf` returns status 37.

rows.name: FAKE_RUNTRON_HOLD
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `runtron` sleeps for `FAKE_RUNTRON_DELAY` seconds and exits.
rows.effect: Keeps the fake `runtron` running until it receives `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM`.
rows.notes: `FAKE_RUNTRON_DELAY` and `FAKE_RUNTRON_EXIT` then have no effect. The signal handler exits with status 0.

rows.name: FAKE_STATE
rows.values: Path of an existing directory.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `traced`, `traced_probes`, `perfetto` and `runtron` stop with an unbound-variable error. These scripts run with `set -eu`.
rows.effect: Names the directory where the fake programs write process ids, arguments and marker files for the tests.
rows.notes: The test fixture sets it to the directory `state` under its temporary directory. The tests read the files to check what the launcher scripts `perfetto/tronperf` and `perfetto/wrapper` did.

rows.name: FAKE_SUDO_FAIL
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `sudo` makes its last argument writable.
rows.effect: Makes the fake `sudo` write its arguments to `sudo.args` and exit with status 73, with no permission change.
rows.notes: Only the fake `sudo` of the test `test_tracefs_repair_is_limited_to_exact_trusted_default` reads it. The script tests it before `FAKE_SUDO_NO_EFFECT` and `FAKE_SUDO_RACE`.

rows.name: FAKE_SUDO_NO_EFFECT
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `sudo` makes its last argument writable.
rows.effect: Makes the fake `sudo` write its arguments to `sudo.args` and exit with status 0, with no permission change.
rows.notes: Only the fake `sudo` of the test `test_tracefs_repair_is_limited_to_exact_trusted_default` reads it. The test checks that `prepare_tracefs` in `perfetto/launcher-common` then fails with status 1.

rows.name: FAKE_SUDO_RACE
rows.values: Path of a directory that the script creates. Any non-empty text turns it on.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `sudo` only makes its last argument writable.
rows.effect: After its permission change, the fake `sudo` creates this directory and sends `SIGTERM` to its parent process.
rows.notes: The test passes the path of the directory `instances/tron` in its fake tracefs (the kernel tracing file system). It checks that the directory still exists after the run.

rows.name: FAKE_TRACED_CAPTURE_MARKER
rows.values: File name relative to the `FAKE_STATE` directory.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `traced` does not wait for a marker file.
rows.effect: Names a file that the fake `traced` waits for before the exit that `FAKE_TRACED_EXIT_AFTER_CAPTURE_READY` requests.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when `FAKE_TRACED_EXIT_AFTER_CAPTURE_READY` is not empty. The test passes `runtron.pid`.

rows.name: FAKE_TRACED_CLOSE_DELAY
rows.values: Number of seconds. The script passes the text to `sleep` unchanged.
rows.default: Unset: 0 seconds.
rows.effect: Sets how long the fake `traced` sleeps between the readiness byte and the close of its notify descriptor.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when `TRACED_NOTIFY_FD` is set and `FAKE_TRACED_CLOSE_READY_FD` is empty. With `FAKE_TRACED_HOLD_READY_FD` the script sleeps and then keeps the descriptor open.

rows.name: FAKE_TRACED_CLOSE_READY_FD
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `traced` writes the readiness byte.
rows.effect: Makes the fake `traced` close its notify descriptor without a readiness byte. No test sets it.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when `TRACED_NOTIFY_FD` is set. The matching switch of the fake `traced_probes` is `FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_CLOSE_READY_FD`. One test sets that switch.

rows.name: FAKE_TRACED_EXIT_AFTER_CAPTURE_READY
rows.values: Exit status, an integer. Any non-empty text turns it on. The script passes the text to `exit` unchanged.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `traced` runs until a signal stops it.
rows.effect: Makes the fake `traced` exit with this status after the fake `perfetto` has reported readiness.
rows.notes: The script waits until `perfetto.ready` exists in the `FAKE_STATE` directory. It also waits for the file that `FAKE_TRACED_CAPTURE_MARKER` names, when that is set. The test passes `71`.

rows.name: FAKE_TRACED_HOLD_READY_FD
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `traced` closes its notify descriptor after the readiness byte.
rows.effect: Makes the fake `traced` keep its notify descriptor open after it writes the readiness byte.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when `TRACED_NOTIFY_FD` is set and `FAKE_TRACED_CLOSE_READY_FD` is empty. The test sets it to `1` with `TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT` set to `1`. It checks that the launcher script `perfetto/tronperf` exits with status 1.

rows.name: FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_CAPTURE_MARKER
rows.values: File name relative to the `FAKE_STATE` directory.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `traced_probes` does not wait for a marker file.
rows.effect: Names a file that the fake `traced_probes` waits for before the exit that `FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_EXIT_AFTER_CAPTURE_READY` requests.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when `FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_EXIT_AFTER_CAPTURE_READY` is not empty. The test passes `runtron.pid` for the launcher script `perfetto/tronperf` and `killall.args` for the launcher script `perfetto/wrapper`.

rows.name: FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_CLOSE_READY_FD
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `traced_probes` writes the readiness byte.
rows.effect: Makes the fake `traced_probes` close its notify descriptor without a readiness byte.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when `TRACED_PROBES_NOTIFY_FD` is set. The test checks that the launcher script `perfetto/tronperf` then exits with status 1.

rows.name: FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_EXIT_AFTER_CAPTURE_READY
rows.values: Exit status, an integer. Any non-empty text turns it on, `0` included. The script passes the text to `exit` unchanged.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `traced_probes` runs until a signal stops it.
rows.effect: Makes the fake `traced_probes` exit with this status after the fake `perfetto` has reported readiness.
rows.notes: The script waits until `perfetto.ready` exists in the `FAKE_STATE` directory. It also waits for the file that `FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_CAPTURE_MARKER` names, when that is set. The test passes `73` and `0`.

rows.name: FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_EXIT_AFTER_READY
rows.values: Exit status, an integer. Any non-empty text turns it on. The script passes the text to `exit` unchanged.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `traced_probes` runs until a signal stops it.
rows.effect: Makes the fake `traced_probes` exit with this status after the fake `perfetto` has started.
rows.notes: The script first reports its own readiness. Then it waits until `perfetto.pid` exists in the `FAKE_STATE` directory. The script tests this variable before `FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_EXIT_AFTER_CAPTURE_READY`.

new_terms.definition: A short script that a test writes in place of a real program, for example `perfetto`, `runtron`, `sudo`, `git` or `gh`. The test puts it where the code under test looks for the real program.
The three Perfetto programs that the launchers start: the tracing service, the probes daemon and the client that records the trace.

The two launcher scripts for Perfetto traces. `perfetto/tronperf` starts the Perfetto programs and then runtron. `perfetto/wrapper` starts the Perfetto programs and can send `SIGUSR1` to a running process.
One byte that a Perfetto program writes to a file descriptor to report that it is ready. The launcher passes that descriptor, named the notify descriptor here.
The kernel tracing file system. The launchers use `/sys/kernel/tracing`.

notes: All 24 variables are fixtures. Only fake programs that two test files write read them. FAKE_TRACED_CLOSE_READY_FD has an empty set_in: the fake traced script reads it and no test sets it. Four evidence quotes are a part of their source line, cut to leave out the shell operator made of two pipe characters: the read sites of FAKE_SUDO_FAIL, FAKE_SUDO_NO_EFFECT, FAKE_SUDO_RACE (second line) and FAKE_TRACED_HOLD_READY_FD. All other quotes are the whole line without the indent. Fixture rows also carry values and default, taken from the script text.
